line: Checked November 19, 2026: all 52 checks passed, against the study's own code (study/common.py), its committed files, and the paper's printed numbers.

the four measurement names are UCI's, in order (data/iris/iris.names)
the three species are the file's classes, in the study's (sorted) order
the families and their s for d = 4 are study/common.py's

the paper's numbers in the data equal paper/numbers.tex
37 of the study's 100 Eq. 4 draws at k = 2 had a zero column, as the paper prints
the plate's petal rows are petal length and petal width
the data names the files it was read from
the page's min-max scaling equals scikit-learn's MinMaxScaler on the study's Iris
every matrix equals study/common.py's projection_matrix on the same G and U (40,000 matrices)
X R / sqrt(k) in the page equals study/common.py's project (600 matrices, 150 flowers each)
the flowers span exactly rank(R) dimensions (numpy's matrix_rank of the projected cloud)
the rank the sentences use equals numpy's matrix_rank (30,000 matrices)
Gaussian entries have mean 0 (3,600,000 entries)
Gaussian entries have variance 1
Gaussian entries follow the standard normal law (Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance times sqrt(n), 200,000 entries; 1.95 is the 0.1% critical value)
Eq. 3's entries take exactly the study's values (−1.0000000000000000, +1.0000000000000000)
Eq. 3's entries have the study's probabilities (3,600,000 entries)

Eq. 4's entries have the study's probabilities (3,600,000 entries)

One per column's entries have the study's probabilities (3,600,000 entries)
the sparse matrices are masks of the same signs (every family's nonzero entries have G's sign; 20,000 cards)
k = 2 uses the first two columns of the k = 3 matrix, as in the study
a card drawn again from its seed is the same card (2,000 cards)
consecutive cards of a seed differ
theory for Eq. 4 at k = 2: a zero column 35.6%, as the paper prints (z:theory_zero_iris = 35.6)
theory for Eq. 4 at k = 2: both petal rows zero 19.8%, as the paper prints (z:theory_both_iris = 19.8)
the theory equals exact enumeration over every zero pattern (5 families, k = 2 and 3)
the formulas the plate writes out evaluate to its theory values
sampled shares of both events land within 4 standard errors of theory (300,000 draws per setting)
the 95% band equals SciPy's binomial quantiles (220 cases)

at least 95% of runs land on the whole counts each band's sentence prints, both ends included, by SciPy's binomial law, and its rounded shares hold every count in it (220 cases; three draws of Eq. 4 at k = 3, both petal rows zero: 0 to 1 of 3, 97.8% of runs; one draw of Eq. 4 at k = 2: all of them)
shares round half up to one decimal as paper/make_numbers.py does (49,450 shares)
coordinates round half up to two decimals as the paper's rnd does (18,000 values)
every dropped-measurement sentence names exactly the all-zero rows, and the rest as used (240,000 draws)
every column sentence names exactly the all-zero columns and how many dimensions the projected flowers span
every branch of the two sentences occurs in the sample (16 branches)
each family's sentence states the study's values, probabilities, and s
every tally sentence and label carries its run's counts, shares, theory, and band (600 simulated runs)
the tally counts each of the reader's draws, with its zero column and petal rows, and none of the 16,715 cards the plate draws on its own (600 simulated runs)
every flower readout reads the flower's file values and its scaled and projected coordinates (3,000 readouts)
the chapter page carries the plate, its data file, and its script
the model checked here is the one in the site's source

the address's seed is its decimal digits, read exactly and taken modulo 2^32, and anything else is no seed (18 addresses: ?seed=9007199254740993 is seed 1, ?seed=4294967296 and ?seed=0 are seed 0, and ?seed=7abc, -0, 42.5, and 6e3 are none); the plate's ?seed= link reads back as the same seed and cards (403 links)
the bars' short labels are the model's counts, and with no draws of the reader's in the tally, after a reset or the plate's own cards, they say "no draws of yours" (no "yet")

the notes on the families and on changing a setting say what the plate does: the Gaussian family is G itself and the others take G's signs and U's mask; once a card exists, a change keeps its G and U, with the chosen family's rule and the first k columns (2,000 cards; the mask stays the same from Gaussian to Eq. 3 on 2,000 and from Eq. 4 to very sparse at k = 2 on 457, so it promises no different mask)

the seed line promises cards by number, with the same matrix for the same family and k, and names the plate's own cards, on the built view. Expected: unseeded at seed 42, the plate draws cards 1 and 2 on its own and the reader's first draw is card 3; at its link, ?seed=42, the plate draws only card 1 on its own, two draws reach card 3, and the line says to reload, with no link to the address already open; on both visits, the view's radio inputs then make each of the 50 changes one radio can make (at each k, each family to each other family; in each family, each k to the other), one change event each, and after every event card 3 prints the entries of seed 42's card 3 for the family and k then chosen, under the seed line and link the visit showed before its first change; ?seed=4294967296 shows seed 0 and links ?seed=0. Seen: 2 and 1 cards drawn on their own, first draw card 3, card 3 after two draws, 50 and 50 of the 50 changes made, and those entries and that line after 95 of 95 and 95 of 95 change events
